<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
Change `TimeTriggeredUniverseSubscriptionEnumeratorFactory` processing on universe 's CollectionChanged to sync new subscriptions with the next timestep.

This lead to necessary changes to a few regressions because their behaviour is related to the bug.

Also one change to `BacktestResultHandler` where sampling was directly adding points to series, now it uses Series.AddPoint() which verifies the validity of the point before entering. This was a breaking issue post changes because of a duplicate keys being entered into Series value.

#### Related Issue
<!--- This project only accepts pull requests related to open issues -->
<!--- If suggesting a new feature or change, please discuss it in an issue first -->
<!--- If fixing a bug, there should be an issue describing it with steps to reproduce -->
<!--- Please link to the issue here: -->
Closes #4757 


#### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
In order to synchronize data that is added outside of initialize with the next timestep I had to bump the time on the collection by 1 tick so that it doesn't generate a point for the current time thus triggering OnData for a given time more than once.

Here is an example of the issue:

```
        private bool _called = false;

        public override void Initialize()
        {
            SetStartDate(2014, 06, 05);  //Set Start Date
            AddEquity("SPY", Resolution.Minute);

            UniverseSettings.Resolution = Resolution.Daily;
        }

        public override void OnData(Slice data)
        {
            var symbols = data.Bars.Keys.Select(x => x.Value).ToList();
            Log($"Add Equity Called: {_called} : {Time} : "+ string.Join(" ", symbols));
            if (!_called)
            {
                AddEquity("AAPL", Resolution.Minute);
                _called = true;
            }
            else if (Time.Equals(new DateTime(2014, 06, 5, 12, 0, 0)))
            {
                RemoveSecurity("AAPL");
            }
        }
```

##### Before Changes:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41277998/96633223-ad4c8180-12cd-11eb-9466-8c55ede31e0d.png)

As you can see, AAPL is added at 9:31AM and then OnData gets triggered again for 9:31AM in the next loop. Instead we should see it not show until 9:32AM in Sync with the next SPY data.

##### After Changes:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41277998/96633698-52fff080-12ce-11eb-8f40-2c5f16be2f7e.png)

Now the data is synced with SPY and we do not pass through OnData twice with the same timestamp. 

I can also confirm that removal still works as expected, I put a condition that if it was a removal action to not alter the time.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41277998/96633912-9fe3c700-12ce-11eb-80bc-4869bcf11fae.png)

 


#### Requires Documentation Change
<!--- Please indicate if these changes will require updates to documentation, and if so, specify what changes are required -->

N/A

#### How Has This Been Tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->

All regressions are passing and those that needed adjustments have been altered. Travis tests run locally in docker also all pass.

pr_comments:
Ideally, this could be fixed closer to the source of the bug. I feel like the root bug is the start time of the subscription is being set to a value in the "past" and not "now" so it is not filtering a bar that should be filtered. By the time we have finished OnData even in backtesting some time has passed so it is already 0931.050. It might be some start time of the subscription on the config to allow this.

Fixing in a universe factory with added tick feels too far from that root cause. But for posterity it's here because there is no start time on the configuration files created when AddSecurity is called; and its start time is set by that universe Collection Change event. I hope in 2 years I hope we understand why we're adding a tick here :)

issue_context.title: Synchronization After Newly Added Securities
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
After a Security is added, the next iteration has a different date/time and synchronized data.

#### Actual Behavior
After a Security is added, the next iteration repeats the date/time and doesn't have synchronized data.

#### Potential Solution
Add new securities with start date/time greater than the current algorithm time. 

#### Reproducing the Problem
```python
class TestingAlgorithm(QCAlgorithm):
    def Initialize(self):
        self.SetStartDate(2020, 9, 22)
        self.SetEndDate(self.StartDate)
        self.AddEquity('SPY')
        
    def OnData(self, slice):
        if self.Time.hour == 9 and self.Time.minute < 33:
            self.Log(f'Time before calling AddEquity: {self.Time} ' + ' '.join([x.Value for x in slice.Bars.Keys]))
            self.AddEquity('QQQ')
            self.Log(f'Time after calling AddEquity: {self.Time} ' + ' '.join([x.Value for x in slice.Bars.Keys]))
```
Output
```
2020-09-22 09:31:00 Time before calling AddEquity: 2020-09-22 09:31:00 SPY
2020-09-22 09:31:00 Time after calling AddEquity: 2020-09-22 09:31:00 SPY
2020-09-22 09:31:00 Time before calling AddEquity: 2020-09-22 09:31:00 QQQ
2020-09-22 09:31:00 Time after calling AddEquity: 2020-09-22 09:31:00 QQQ
2020-09-22 09:32:00 Time before calling AddEquity: 2020-09-22 09:32:00 QQQ SPY
2020-09-22 09:32:00 Time after calling AddEquity: 2020-09-22 09:32:00 QQQ SPY
```
